lines.text: This space telescope is about to fall out of the sky.
NASA has ended the science mission of Swift. It launched in 2004, built to last just two years. It ran for nearly 22.
Its job: catch gamma-ray bursts, some of the most powerful explosions in the universe, and swing its telescopes onto them in about a minute, before the glow fades.
It caught more than 2,000 of them, plus over 1,400 supernovae.
So why stop? An active Sun puffed up Earth's upper atmosphere. The extra drag kept pulling Swift lower, and it has no engine to climb back up.
A robotic spacecraft was launched to boost it higher. But it ran into trouble, and the rescue failed.
On October 20, Swift made its final observation. NASA expects it to re-enter the atmosphere within weeks.
But its 12 terabytes of data stay public, for anyone to explore.
